ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended, together with the Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information, Joint Order No. 3 of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Management of Customer Identification and Customer Identity and Transaction Records in Financial Institutions; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Hong Kong Cap. 615) and Companies Ordinance (Hong Kong Cap. 622) for the Hong Kong shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Continuing Registration of the Hong Kong shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention route: registry certificate notarized by a Hong Kong notary public and then apostilled by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR; no consular legalization for any Apostille Convention destination. Non-member state route: notarization, government authentication, and consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive paths and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency relating to the Hong Kong shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry and the licensed corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention route: current status report notarized and apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court. Non-member state route: current status report notarized, authenticated by the competent Hong Kong authority, and legalized by the destination consulate. The two authentication routes are parallel alternatives; sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the PRC WFOE, bank account opening and foreign investment filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Hong Kong shareholder (certified by the company secretary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention route: certified board resolution and power of attorney notarized and apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court. Non-member state route: notarization, authentication by the competent Hong Kong authority, and consular legalization. Use one path only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention route: certified copy of the registered memorandum and articles notarized and apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court. Non-member destination: certified copy notarized, authenticated, and consular legalized. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter covering the Hong Kong shareholder's source of funds and compliance standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sole-licensed commercial bank maintaining the Hong Kong company's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention route: bank reference letter signed by the branch or relationship manager, notarized, and apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court. Non-member route: bank reference letter notarized, authenticated, and legalized at the destination consulate. No document may undergo both apostille and consular legalization in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories and material counterparties of both the Hong Kong investor and the PRC WFOE must be screened before incorporation against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK HM Treasury sanctions, FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists, PRC Ministry of Public Security and People's Bank of China watch lists, and Hong Kong Customs and Excise anti-money-laundering records. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be identified through commercial databases, beneficial ownership declarations and in-person interviews. Any PEP match requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source of wealth and source of funds verification, adverse media review and ongoing transaction monitoring. Any sanctions or criminal-association match mandates immediate rejection, suspicious transaction reporting and termination of the incorporation project.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and SAMR online Enterprise Name Reservation and Market Entity Registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE statutory name must be composed exclusively in Simplified Chinese characters and must conform to the four-tier naming formula: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business-operation characteristic, and organization form. English names, Pinyin, traditional Chinese characters and Latin script are not acceptable in the registered Chinese legal name. The foreign investor's

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 effective revision), Articles 16, 20, 27-29, 39-42, 47-50, 76 and 147; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 20, 23, 30 and 31
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Registration Bureau, acting through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association of Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise and Application for Business License (Form A) submitted to SAMR
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The PRC Company Law does not impose a statutory minimum registered capital for ordinary limited liability companies or WFOEs engaged in software publishing. The capital contribution amount is determined by the investors and recorded in the Articles of Association; contributions must be made according to the schedule set out in the Articles, with no requirement for an escrowed blocked account unless the capital is used for an activity requiring prior approval. The maximum subscription period must be specified and must be consistent with the Company's operational plan.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD (adopted by written consent in lieu of a meeting on [date], 2025 at the registered office). PRESENT: the subscribing shareholders and the persons designated as the inaugural officers. RESOLVED: (1) The Board confirms that the registered capital of the Company shall be [amount in RMB] yuan, divided into [number] shares of equal nominal value. The Board accepts the subscription statements of the founding shareholders, orders that the subscription amounts be reflected in the capitalization plans, and directs each shareholder to pay the applicable consideration either in full at closing or in instalments strictly on the dates set out in the Contribution Schedule approved by these resolutions. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be adopted as the Department of Market Supervision Administration address specified in the Articles of Association, and the Legal Representative is authorized to execute the lease and all documents required to register such office with the competent SAMR authority. (3) The following officers are appointed for an initial term of three years, or as otherwise specified in the Articles: (a) [Name] of [address] as Executive Director, Chairperson of the Board and Legal Representative of the Company; (b) [Name] as Supervisor and chair of the supervisory body; (c) [Name] as General Manager, Company Secretary and Chief Compliance Officer. Each statutory officer is accountable to the Board and has the fiduciary duties of honesty and diligence imposed by Article 147 of the PRC Company Law. (4) The General Manager is empowered to open, operate, close and mandate accounts in the name of the Company with any licensed commercial bank in China, particularly the basic RMB settlement account and the foreign currency capital and current accounts. The bank is requested to act on written instructions bearing the joint signature of the General Manager and the Legal Representative, or the sole signature of the General Manager for transactions not exceeding fifty thousand yuan, in accordance with the Delegated Authority Matrix. (5) The Legal Representative is directed to file all foreign exchange registration forms and direct investment information with SAFE through the designated bank, and to ensure that the proceeds from commercial publishing agreements with Valve Corporation (Steam) and Sony Interactive Entertainment (PlayStation Store) are received in the foreign exchange current account and settled in accordance with RMB exchange rate regulations. (6) The Board approves, ratifies and adopts the professional fees of the formation counsel, notaries, translation bureau and the official legalization charges as proper expenses of the Company, which shall be paid out of the first capital funds. (7) The Board confirms that these resolutions may be relied upon by the Company's bankers, the SAMR, SAFE and the taxation authorities as the final and binding expression of the Company's will, and that all prior draft resolutions are superseded. The meeting was closed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) Name Registration Window and Online Enterprise Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the SAMR online platform or one-stop municipal government service hall, the founder submits three proposed company names in Chinese and English. The name check engine will run a nationwide conflict scan and an automatic compliance review against the negative list for foreign-invested enterprise access. If no conflict, a Certificate of Enterprise Name Pre-approval is issued online. The certificate is valid for six months and must be presented in the subsequent incorporation filing. In case of conflict or substantive refusal, the applicant may rely on the adverse action remedies detailed below.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Name Pre-approval Application Form
Passport or ID copies of all shareholders
Power of attorney (if filed through agent)
No-objection letter from the local commercial space provider (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on conflict or negative list grounds, the applicant may file a fresh name application online within the same business day or submit a written objection to the local SAMR name review division; a formal rejection letter must be cured by amending the proposed name and resubmitting, which restarts the SLA clock at three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration Global Services Window and accredited Courthouse Notary Office for foreign shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a PRC-licensed formation agent and notary to prepare the Articles of Association, the shareholder subscription agreement, and the appointment resolution. Every signature of foreign shareholders must be notarized by a notary public and legalized by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate, or apostilled where the Apostille Convention applies; all documents in a language other than Chinese must be translated and certified. Submit the full package to the local Market Supervision Administration for pre-review through the Global Services window. Ensure the business scope is delineated as development and publishing of self-developed computer and console video games via digital platforms, online and mobile gaming licensing and operation. If the SAMR queries the scope, the category codes IC 5820 and NAICS 511210 can be referenced to avoid license over-regulation.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of parent company (for foreign investor)
Consular legalization or apostille of corporate documents
Articles of Association drafted in Chinese
Shareholders subscription and contribution declaration
Lease agreement for registered office in China
Name pre-approval certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarization package is queried due to incomplete legalization or translation errors, the applicant corrects the deficient exhibit and re-submits to the Global Services window within the statutory cure period; the SAMR pre-review clock restarts upon the corrected submission, with a maximum extension of five additional working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Enterprise Registration Bureau and Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving station
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for incorporation through the integrated State Administration for Market Regulation portal. The registry will issue a formal acceptance receipt and a unique application number. The registrar verifies that the Articles comply with the minimum statutory content under Article 25 of the PRC Company Law and that the registered capital subscription period is stated. Upon approval, the enterprise business license is electronically generated with a unified social credit code, and the Company is entered into the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. After issuance, the legal representative proceeds to a licensed seal engraving shop to produce the official composite seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and invoice seal, each of which must be filed at the local public security organ.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of company establishment
Articles of Association
Name approval certificate
Proof of legal person identity
Consent of office use signed by the landlord and property ownership certificate
Foreign investor qualification certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for missing documents, the applicant receives a Notice of Supplemental Submission; after uploading the missing document, the clock restarts from the date of completion, with two additional working days for final adjudication. If the business license is rejected due to scope inconsistency, the applicant may file an internal administrative review with the same SAMR bureau or re-file a revised Articles of Association within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Insurance and Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax service hall, municipal social insurance bureau, and SAFE through designated banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days of obtaining the business license, the General Manager must register the Company for corporate income tax, value-added tax, individual income tax withholding, stamp duty and social insurance contributions with the local branch of the State Taxation Administration and the municipal social insurance registration center. The Company's foreign investor must report direct investment information to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange via the qualifying bank's capital information system before any capital injection or profit repatriation. If the Company will receive US-dollar settlements from Steam or PlayStation, the transaction code should not be designated as cross-border e-commerce but as royalty income or software license fees to align with SAFE and bank review expectations, thereby ensuring compliant collection of proceeds.
required_dossiers: Business license unified social credit code certificate
Tax registration form and bank account information
Beneficial owner declaration
Social insurance registration form
Foreign investment information report (through SAFE online system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to register tax on time triggers a late-filing fine, but correction can be made online via the STA e-tax platform; a written explanation and payment of the late fee cure the defect. For SAFE reporting errors, the corrective report can be filed with the designated bank's foreign exchange operations department within ten working days without reinstating the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank branch with SAFE foreign exchange qualification and the People's Bank of China payment settlement system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The General Manager and Legal Representative attend the chosen bank in person with the original enterprise business license, the notarized items listed below, the board resolution authorizing banking, and the registered office proof. For the capital account, the bank will require the Foreign Investment Business Registration Certificate issued by SAFE's online system and will wire the subscription amount from the foreign shareholder's overseas account to the Company's local foreign currency capital account. Once the capital is received, the bank issues a Foreign Exchange Bank Receipt, which must be kept for the audited annual compliance report. A basic settlement account in RMB should be opened separately to manage operational receivables including the periodic Steam and PlayStation remittances. All accounts must be linked to the tax filing record.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Articles of Association
First board resolution authorizing banking arrangements
Company seal and legal representative seal
Foreign Investment Business Registration Certificate (SAFE)
Registered office proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to limitations on foreign exchange account opening, the company may reapply to another SAFE-licensed bank after updating the lease agreement and providing an additional board resolution; if the refusal is grounded on anti-money laundering risk findings, submit an AML remediation package including the ultimate beneficial owner chart and source-of-funds statement to the bank's compliance department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital software publishing and online distribution activity under ISIC 5820; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation in China
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial production permit required for a digital storefront publishing model; no physical license under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology or municipal industrial board is triggered for a wholly foreign-owned software publisher that does not operate a manufacturing plant

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - entity is not a physical factory; no Environmental Impact Assessment categorization is required because the WFOE will not generate industrial wastewater, air emissions, solid hazardous waste, or noise exceeding environmental permitting thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no production effluent, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams exist; the only compliance applicable is ordinary office waste disposal under municipal waste management regulations, which requires no EIA tier

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no manufacturing floor, warehouse, chemical storage, or high-occupancy production facility exists; therefore no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety production license is required. The WFOE is limited to leasing a Class B office space that must only comply with ordinary office fire safety rules enforced by the building management and the local fire rescue bureau.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) and its local tax services; online portal: China Electronic Tax Bureau (etax.chinatax.gov.cn), including the Export Tax Rebate (Exemption) module and the electronic invoice issuing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE is incorporated with the Administration for Market Regulation and automatically receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which constitutes the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for PRC tax purposes. The market regulator pushes the incorporation record to the STA, effecting automatic tax registration. The legal representative and appointed financial officer must then log on to the China Electronic Tax Bureau to complete the new-taxpayer confirmation, install the tax UKey/digital certificate, elect VAT taxpayer status (general or small-scale), activate electronic invoice issuance authority, and register the correct tax types. No additional VAT registration certificate is issued. Non-resident shareholders do not require a separate PRC TIN solely to own the WFOE; if the non-resident person has direct PRC-source income or a permanent establishment, a separate withholding registration/procedure is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not recognise US-style check-the-box entity classification and provides no elective hybrid mismatch treatment. A WFOE is mandatorily treated as a PRC resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income. The only indirect-tax election available is voluntary registration as a general VAT taxpayer where annual taxable turnover is below the CNY 5,000,000 threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover; all WFOEs with a business license are tax-registered upon incorporation, and exceeding this threshold makes general VAT taxpayer registration mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Fully digitalized electronic invoices are used under the Golden Tax Phase IV system. VAT special invoices must be issued through the China Electronic Tax Bureau, signed with the taxpayer's tax UKey, assigned a unique electronic invoice number, and uploaded to the STA in real time. Invoice data is automatically cross-checked with customs declarations, foreign-exchange receipts, and input-credit claims. Anti-fraud controls include digital signatures, tax-control codes, and mandatory electronic reconciliation before a special VAT invoice may be used.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where the WFOE exports physical goods out of the PRC customs territory or supplies qualifying cross-border taxable services, including digital software publishing/licensing to Valve, PlayStation Store, or overseas end customers. The supply must be received and consumed outside China, the payment must be received in foreign currency by the WFOE, and the transaction must be correctly reported in the China Electronic Tax Bureau as a zero-rated/export supply. Pure digital downloads do not have a customs border crossing; for such supplies the statutory documentation is the cross-border service contract, platform payout/settlement statements, and foreign-exchange receipts rather than a physical export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: PRC Customs Export Goods Declaration Form bearing the export declaration number and customs clearance record (required for physical media/goods exports)
Bill of Lading or sea/air waybill issued by the carrier evidencing export from a PRC customs port (not required for pure digital services)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued foreign exchange receipt confirmation from the SAFE trade monitoring system evidencing the Valve/PlayStation payout to the WFOE
Export sale, copyright licensing, or digital publishing agreement with the overseas platform/licensee
Steamworks or PlayStation Partner payout statements reconciled with invoices, customs declarations, and foreign-exchange receipts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA compares export declarations, electronic invoices, foreign-exchange receipts, contracts, and platform statements through the Golden Tax IV risk-control system. If the zero-rating is unsubstantiated, proceeds are received late without an approved extension, or domestic digital sales are misstated as exports, the STA will restore VAT liability with retrospective effect, charge late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day, impose an administrative penalty of up to five times the tax involved for fraudulent export refund claims, downgrade the export tax-rebate credit rating, and refer egregious cases for criminal prosecution for export-tax-refund fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the delegated foreign-exchange authority of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the PRC foreign-exchange control framework, the Renminbi is broadly convertible for current-account trade and service transactions but remains strictly managed on the capital account. The WFOE must complete SAFE's direct-investment foreign-exchange registration through its designated settlement bank before receiving any equity capital. Inbound capital must enter a segregated FDI capital account and may be settled into RMB only under the pay-use model with a negative list; prohibited uses include repayment of existing offshore loans, entrusted loans, securities investments, purchase of wealth-management products, real-estate purchases outside the approved scope, and non-business-related foreign-exchange speculation. Current-account receipts from Steam and console-store publishing are treated as cross-border service-trade income after documentary authenticity verification by the receiving bank; the bank will review the publishing agreement, platform payout statements, tax filing records and the SAFE payment-purpose declaration. Dividend remittances to the Hong Kong shareholder are conditional on audited annual financial statements, corporate income tax clearance, withholding-tax certificates, a board dividend resolution and current-account dividend-remittance verification. In practical liquidity terms, the bank must be provided with notarized copies of the WFOE's business licence, social-credit code certificate, legal representative identity documents and the SAFE FDI registration code. Because the onshore RMB spot market is managed, settlement is executed at the market middle rate with a bank spread; no free capital-account exchange is available.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory surrender ratio is zero; China abolished mandatory foreign-exchange surrender for current-account trade receipts. The WFOE may either retain export/service proceeds in a foreign-currency settlement account with a SAFE-designated bank or convert them into RMB at prevailing market rates. The legal collection requirement is that proceeds must be repatriated to the domestic settlement account by the payment date specified in the underlying Steam/PlayStation agreement, and any uncollected receivable outstanding more than 90 days after the invoice date must be reported to SAFE through the company's bank with supporting contracts and overdue-receivable explanation. Extension beyond 180 days without an agreed amendment may lead to a trade foreign-exchange monitoring downgrade and restriction to the B/C classification, which forces full settlement and per-document review. All receipts require an income declaration showing the SAFE current-account transaction code, the payer's registration identifier and the associated publishing contract.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are effectively legally barred from acting as the WFOE's principal onshore treasury rail because they do not hold a deposit-taking banking licence from the National Financial Regulatory Administration and are not connected to SAFE's direct-investment and current-account monitoring system. They cannot receive FDI capital, execute SAFE registrations, perform RMB capital settlement, or issue verification-compliant trade receipts in mainland China. An EMI may be used only by an offshore Hong Kong treasury affiliate for collections outside mainland; any transfer of funds back to the WFOE must cross SAFE-controlled banking rails. Overall viability rating is low for primary treasury operations and conditionally medium for offshore collection, pooling or escrow in tandem with a licensed Tier-1 Chinese bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one physical in-branch identity interview is mandatory at the chosen bank's mainland branch. The statutory legal representative or a single authorized executive holding a notarized board resolution and power of attorney must appear in person with original company chops, business licence and legal representative identification. Remote consular proxy opening is not an accepted substitute; although foreign directors may authenticate powers of attorney through Hong Kong consular or notarial channels, the designated individual must still attend the interview in mainland China. Biometric verification and electronic data capture may supplement but will not replace physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Hong Kong shareholder is newly incorporated, has limited operating substance and the ownership chain involves nominee shareholders, creating UBO opacity and cross-border tax-residency ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: updated Hong Kong Business Registration certificate; HK Companies Registry NAR1 annual return; complete shareholders' register and directors' register; valid passports of every individual holding 10% or more; a certified UBO declaration identifying each natural person with ultimate control; group treasury and business rationale memorandum; audited financial statements or a CPA certificate for the Hong Kong shareholder; source-of-wealth evidence for the remitting bank account; notarized corporate authorizations; and the WFOE's internal AML/KYC pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE's Chinese founding team reportedly controls the Hong Kong parent, exposing the group to SAFE Circular 37 registration concerns and possible round-tripping of domestic capital through an offshore conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: SAFE Circular 37 registration certificates for each Chinese-resident shareholder of the Hong Kong vehicle; ODI approval records from MOFCOM and NDRC where the Hong Kong shareholder is a PRC corporate investor; complete funding trail from the original overseas remittance to the Hong Kong shareholder's bank account; Hong Kong tax returns and financial statements for the last two years; bank statements for the remitting account; and written legal counsel confirmation that no PRC domestic assets, deposits or guarantees were used to finance the Hong Kong shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-storefront proceeds from Valve and PlayStation lack traditional customs documentation and are paid in variable monthly baskets, triggering bank concern over authenticity of current-account service-trade receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: original Steam and PlayStation publishing and distribution agreements; platform merchant and developer identifier registrations; monthly settlement statements or payout confirmations issued by Valve and PlayStation; payment-processor export ledger; download and telemetry sales reports; bank incoming remittance records matched to platform payor names; software copyright registration certificates and IP ownership licences; issued tax invoices and business tax payment slips; and a SAFE service-trade current-account income declaration aligned with each receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party royalty and service-fee flows between the WFOE, the Hong Kong parent and the overseas original IP owner may appear as non-arm's-length profit stripping or disguised dividend remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: signed intercompany licensing and service agreements; transfer-pricing local file and a benchmark report supporting the royalty rate; group IP ownership chart including copyright registration assignments; annual China Corporate Income Tax return with the related-party transaction schedule; tax withholding certificates for cross-border fees; invoices and time-entry rate cards for services; board minutes approving royalties and service budgets; and six months of bank statements evidencing that each invoice was paid from an authorized operational account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity from the Hong Kong parent should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's segregated FDI foreign-currency capital account at a Tier-1 designated bank. The remittance instruction must quote the WFOE's unique social-credit code and the SAFE FDI registration certificate reference number, with the purpose stated as inbound direct investment equity injection to a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. The received foreign currency is quarantined from current-account sweep until authenticity verification is completed; the bank then processes the capital-account receipt and, once supporting contracts and use-plan documents are submitted, permits conversion into RMB under the pay-as-you-use capital settlement model. A certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report after the injection is booked, and the WFOE shall update SAFE's foreign-investment register within 30 days. The enterprise should avoid splitting large injections into repeated small transfers because regulatory monitoring thresholds and banking-referral exclusions apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring outbound payments such as Steam platform-hosted royalty distributions, licensing fees to foreign IP owners and PlayStation Store promotion-service fees, use SWIFT MT103 for USD or EUR remittances or CIPS cross-border RMB payment instructions when counterparties accept RMB. The service-export disbursement dossier must contain the signed agreement, tax-withholding certificate, invoice and platform settlement statement. For physical collector's editions and console peripherals, use an irrevocable confirmed letter of credit issued by a Tier-1 Chinese bank or documentary collections such as D/P and D/A; a standby letter of credit is acceptable to support milestone escrow. Direct gaming-revenue remittances should never be routed through a personal account or an unregulated offshore EMI.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts for forward settlement and sale of USD/CNY, specifically covering Steam/PlayStation settlement receipts and licensed dividend obligations; tenor capped at 12 months for current-account trade receipts.

Onshore currency swaps and FX swaps used strictly for cashflow hedging of long-term intercompany receivables or SAFE-registered cross-border intercompany loans; the notional must match the verified outstanding principal and the maximum tenor should not exceed five years unless separately approved by SAFE.

Non-deliverable forward activity is not permitted for the mainland WFOE in onshore practice; an offshore NDF may be considered only by a separately capitalized Hong Kong treasury vehicle and requires documented hedge intent, with no speculative open positions, while all onshore hedging must remain deliverable and supported by genuine trade or capital-account exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (NAR1) under Section 662 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the statutory filing window closes exactly 42 days after the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If delivered late the late fee is HKD 870 (approx. USD 111.54) for up to 3 months; HKD 1,740 (approx. USD 223.08) for more than 3 but not more than 6 months; HKD 2,610 (approx. USD 334.62) for more than 6 but not more than 9 months; and HKD 3,480 (approx. USD 446.15) for more than 9 months. Continued non-filing is an offence subject to a maximum fine of HKD 50,000 (approx. USD 6,410.26) plus daily default fines; the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off and dissolution under Section 746 of the Companies Ordinance where the company appears not to be carrying on business or operation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after the expiry date of the current Business Registration Certificate; alternatively, the 3-year certificate may be renewed every 3 years. The anniversary rule is based on the commencement of business or the prior certificate expiry date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew within the statutory period makes the certificate void and the person carrying on business is liable to prosecution; the maximum fine is HKD 5,000 (approx. USD 641.03) plus a daily fine for continued default. The absence of a valid Business Registration Certificate is treated by the Companies Registry as evidence that the company is not carrying on business and may trigger strike-off and deregistration under Section 746 of the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) together with audited financial statements, tax computation and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where the financial year ends on 31 December, the return is normally issued in April and must be lodged within one month of the issue date; where an authorized tax representative is appointed, an extension to 15 August for paper filing and 15 September for e-filing is generally available. For other accounting reference dates, the IRD computes the due date based on the accounting period and issued-date rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the due date allows the IRD to raise estimated assessments and may result in prosecution; on conviction the company is liable to a fine of up to HKD 10,000 (approx. USD 1,282.05) and a daily default penalty, and additional tax of up to 10% of tax undercharged if the failure is before assessment. Persistent failure to file may be reported by the IRD and can contribute to administrative strike-off proceedings initiated by the Companies Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A) and Employee Particulars (BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date the return is issued; the IRD generally issues the annual employer return in early April and requires it to be filed on or before 1 May immediately following the year of assessment. A nil return must also be filed if no employees were employed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; the company may be fined up to HKD 10,000 (approx. USD 1,282.05) and may be subjected to additional tax of up to 10% of the tax undercharged, with higher penalties where fraud or wilful evasion is established.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register (SCR) Annual Review and In-Year Updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No annual filing is made to the Hong Kong Companies Registry; the register is kept at the company's registered office or prescribed location and is available for inspection by law enforcement officers only.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The register must be updated within 7 days after any change in significant controllers or registrable details; the company secretary should also perform a formal annual review at each financial year-end to ensure the register remains accurate and complete.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the Significant Controllers Register is an offence under the Companies Ordinance; the company and each responsible officer are liable to a fine of up to HKD 25,000 (approx. USD 3,205.13) and a further daily default fine of HKD 700 (approx. USD 89.74) for continued contravention.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Part 9 of the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every company must have its financial statements audited unless it is exempt as a small private company or member of a small private company group. The quantitative small-company test requires satisfaction of at least two of the following three conditions for the financial year: (i) annual revenue not exceeding HKD 100 million (approx. USD 12,820,512.82); (ii) balance-sheet total assets not exceeding HKD 100 million (approx. USD 12,820,512.82); and (iii) average number of employees not exceeding 100. A company that fails to satisfy at least two of those conditions, or that belongs to a group which as a whole

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% statutory enterprise income tax rate under Article 4 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law (“EIT Law”) for all resident enterprises, including the PRC WFOE
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential effective rate reductions available to the WFOE include: 15% reduced rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises; 10% rate for qualifying National Key Software Enterprises; the software enterprise two-year exemption followed by three-year 50% reduction for qualifying newly-established software enterprises; and an additional 100% R&D super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses (total 200% deduction) as currently extended. Any preferential rate must be supported by certificates, core intellectual property, qualifying R&D activities, and genuine mainland China economic substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000, Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Class), filed through the National Electronic Tax Administration (e-tax) portal of the State Taxation Administration; supporting schedules include A105000, A105080, A107012, and the related-party transaction annual disclosure forms where applicable. Outbound dividends, interest, and royalties to the Hong Kong parent are additionally reported on the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return and the Service Trade and Cross-Border Payments tax filing form where amount thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional EIT returns must be filed within 15 days after each quarter-end; the annual final settlement return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (normally 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue from PC and console game publishing through Steam, Steam Deck, PlayStation Store, and related digital storefronts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross revenue recognized under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises 14 net of value-added tax. Reconcile bookings, refunds, platform fees, chargebacks, and Valve/Sony settlement statements. Do not reduce revenue by the non-resident withholding tax or by the Hong Kong parent's profit share; such items are not revenue deductions. Cross-border platform commission expenses must be separately supported by contracts, invoices, and transfer pricing documentation.

Include direct game development amortization, software capitalization amortization, server costs, middleware license fees, and content production costs. Payments to the Hong Kong parent for IP licenses, game balancings, or development services must satisfy the arm's length standard under EIT Law Article 41 and must reflect actual services with retained evidence. Unsupported intercompany IP payments will be adjusted.

Deductible amounts include urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty, and other operating taxes actually paid. Corporate income tax itself and any PRC withholding tax paid to the State Taxation Administration on behalf of the Hong Kong parent are not deductible as enterprise income tax expenses.

Include platform marketing fees, launch promotions, advertising, community management, localisation marketing, and Steam/PlayStation store banner and discovery costs. If the Hong Kong parent invoices marketing services to the WFOE, the WFOE must demonstrate the parent has real marketing personnel and functions outside mainland China; otherwise the fee may be disregarded and treated as a dividend distribution.

Include salaries and welfare for directors, development staff, finance, legal, office rent, utilities, professional fees, and normal business overhead. Management fees charged by the Hong Kong parent are deductible only if the parent has actual functions, risks, employees, and costs, and the fee is computed at arm's length; pure profit-sharing management fees are non-deductible.

Include bank charges, foreign exchange losses, and interest on intercompany loans. Interest paid to the Hong Kong parent must be at arm's length, documented, and subject to the thin-capitalization debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for a non-financial enterprise. Disallowed excess interest must be added back on Schedule A105000. Gross interest paid to the Hong Kong resident parent is subject to PRC withholding tax at 10% statutory rate, reduced to 7% under the Mainland and Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement if the 7% treaty application protocol is satisfied.

Report dividends, interest, and gains from financial assets. Dividends received by the WFOE from another PRC resident enterprise may be exempt under EIT Law Article 26, but dividends from non-resident subsidiaries are taxable and can generate foreign tax credits. This line is not the place to report withholding tax on dividends paid by the WFOE to its Hong Kong parent.

Include government grants, asset surrender gains, penalties received, and other taxable non-operating income. Government subsidies must be reviewed to determine whether they are taxable under EIT Law and the relevant public notices; untaxed subsidy income in a falsified position may constitute an under-reporting red flag.

Recomputed as Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3 minus Box 4 minus Box 5 minus Box 6 plus Box 7 plus Box 8. The accounting profit must reconcile to the audited financial statements and to the Steam/PlayStation remittance reports. Material unexplained deviations between platform settlements and booked revenue are audit triggers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments through Schedule A105000
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible penalties, fines, unsupported entertainment expenses, excess related-party interest, non-arm's length royalties, management fees lacking substance, and prohibited internal depreciation. Deduct R&D super deductions, accelerated depreciation, and other qualifying incentives. Cross-border intragroup payments without paper trails will be denied and may generate deemed withholding liabilities.

Utilize only qualifying carryforward losses within the 5-year statutory limit. Losses generated from offshore platform operations may not be used to reduce taxable income derived in mainland China unless properly recognized. Losses of shell entities without economic substance are disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable and foreign tax credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% statutory rate, then any HNTE or software enterprise preferential rate after certification. For taxable foreign-source income, a foreign tax credit is available but is capped. This line must not be reduced by the PRC withholding tax on the WFOE's dividends to Hong Kong; that withholding is a non-resident taxpayer liability collected by the WFOE as withholding agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of quarterly or annual EIT returns attracts penalties under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law (“TCAL”), generally RMB 2,000, rising to RMB 10,000 for serious cases. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax under TCAL Article 32. Fraudulent underpayment can be sanctioned under TCAL Article 63 with a penalty from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, and criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law can lead to imprisonment and fines. Tax blacklisting triggers travel bans, exit restrictions, and credit restrictions on legal representatives and directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory PRC withholding tax on dividends paid by a PRC resident WFOE to a non-resident corporate shareholder; the rate is reduced to 5% under Article 10 of the Mainland and Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement if the Hong Kong shareholder is a beneficial owner and a Hong Kong tax resident company directly holding at least 25% of the capital of the WFOE.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The WFOE must apply the self-assessment, post-filing documentary procedure under SAT Announcement [2019] No. 35. At the time of dividend payment, the Hong Kong parent must hold a valid Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (Certificate of Resident Status issued by the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department), complete a beneficial owner self-declaration, and provide evidence that the Hong Kong parent has real business substance, employees, offices, decision-making functions, accounting records, and is not a conduit for third-country shareholders. The WFOE should retain the certificate, shareholder register, board minutes, contracts, and proof of dividend resolution in order to withhold at the 5% DTA rate. If the documentation is not complete at payment date, the WFOE should withhold at 10% and the Hong Kong parent may claim a refund through the administrative process under the DTA. Cross-border payments for services, royalties, and interest above the tax filing threshold also require the Service Trade and Cross-Border Payments tax filing form and bank/SAFE documentary review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 10%; the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA reduces the withholding rate to 7% for interest beneficially owned by a Hong Kong resident and to 7% for royalties beneficially owned by a Hong Kong resident. Royalty characterization requires careful analysis of whether payments for game software rights, publishing rights, user databases, or trademark licenses are true royalties or sales of copyrighted articles; mischaracterization as service fees can create a permanent establishment or expose the WFOE to withholding underpayment penalties. Interest on shareholder loans is also subject to the arm's length principle and the 2:1 thin-capitalization ratio, and disallowed interest is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as a dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File is required if annual related-party tangible asset transfers exceed CNY 200 million; intangible asset transfers exceed CNY 100 million; financial asset transfers exceed CNY 100 million; or other related-party transactions including services exceed CNY 40 million. Master File preparation is required where annual related-party transactions exceed CNY 1 billion or where the ultimate parent group is required to prepare a Master File. The related-party transaction disclosure schedules must be filed with the annual CIT return whenever any related-party transaction occurs, regardless of amount.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The mainland WFOE is not subject to a standalone Economic Substance Regulations code equivalent to offshore financial centres, but the substance-over-form doctrine applies through EIT Law Article 47 general anti-avoidance, SAT Announcement [2019] No. 35 beneficial-owner requirements, and PRC case law under the Civil Code and Company Law. The Hong Kong parent must show that its Core Income-Generating Activities for holding the WFOE shares, funding the WFOE, licensing IP, or receiving dividends are actually performed in Hong Kong: meetings, negotiations, contracts, financing decisions, accounting, and treasury functions. The WFOE, in turn, must have real physical premises, employees, payroll, board decisions, and documented operations in China for game development, localisation, Steam/PlayStation publishing relationships, platform settlement, customer support, and content updates. If either entity is a hollow shell or the Shanghai/Hong Kong structure exists mainly to obtain treaty benefits, tax authorities may disregard the structure, impose withholding, reassess profits, and deny treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA abuse and artificial Hong Kong shell company used to obtain 5% dividend withholding relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong shareholder is a bare nominee or shell with no staff, office, economic activity, core functions, bank accounts, or real decision-making; the WFOE nonetheless pays dividends to it and applies the 5% Mainland-Hong Kong DTA rate rather than the 10% statutory rate. Alternatively, the Hong Kong parent immediately passes the dividend onward to ultimate shareholders in a third jurisdiction without retaining economic ownership or control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC tax authority may deny treaty benefits under SAT Announcement [2019] No. 35 and apply the general anti-avoidance rule under EIT Law Article 47. Under TCAL Article 63, the underpaid withholding of 5% plus interest is recovered, and a penalty from 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax can be imposed. If criminal tax evasion is established under Criminal Law Article 201, the punishment is up to three years imprisonment and fines, or up to seven years for large amounts or other serious circumstances. The entity and the responsible directors are jointly exposed to criminal fines and per-person liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under PRC Company Law Article 23 where shareholders abuse corporate personality to evade debts or taxes and seriously harm creditors or state interests. Directors who approved the sham dividend structure or false beneficial-owner declarations can be ordered to make personal asset restitution, be named on the tax-related serious dishonesty blacklist, suffer exit/travel bans and restrictions from leaving mainland China, and face criminal prosecution as directly responsible persons under Criminal Law Articles 30 and 201.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing and economic substance fraud in Steam/PlayStation digital publishing revenue flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE routes a material part of Steam and PlayStation store gross profit to the Hong Kong parent through excessive royalties, manufactured IP purchase prices, artificial management fees, mark-ups on marketing services, or high-interest intercompany loans. No contemporaneous Local File or Master File is prepared despite breaching the CN thresholds; the related-party schedules are not filed with the annual CIT return; and the WFOE claims all economic substance and R&D incentives inside mainland China despite the Hong Kong parent performing no real functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust profits under EIT Law Article 41 and assess taxable income by estimation under EIT Law Article 44 where documentation is absent or false. Under EIT Law Article 48 and the Implementation Regulations, an interest charge is added at the prevailing central bank benchmark loan interest rate plus 5 percentage points for transfer pricing adjustments. Failure to file returns and supplementary schedules is penalized under TCAL Article 62 with fines of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, but deliberate false under-reporting escalates to TCAL Article 63 tax evasion penalties of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the financial controller who sign false financial statements or direct the suppression of taxable revenue may be personally liable for tax restitution through civil joint liability under PRC Company Law Article 23 and Civil Code Article 1168. As directly responsible officers of a unit crime, they may face criminal fines and imprisonment for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, prohibitions on serving as directors or senior managers, and blacklist measures restricting exit, passports, business registration changes, and high-consumption activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold PRC tax on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties to Hong Kong and circumvention of cross-border payment disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends, pays interest, or pays royalties to the Hong Kong parent without withholding the required 10% or 7% non-resident enterprise income tax; or it mischaracterizes dividend payments as offshore services, commissions, or repayments of shareholder loans; or it fails to file the Service Trade and Cross-Border Payments tax filing form before remitting funds exceeding the threshold to Hong Kong; or it provides false beneficial-owner declarations to the bank or tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TCAL Article 69, a withholding agent that fails to withhold or fails to obtain and remit tax is subject to a penalty from 50% to 300% of the amount that should have been withheld, in addition to recovery of the underlying tax from the non-resident taxpayer where collectible. Late payment surcharges accrue under TCAL Article 32. If the mischaracterization is used to avoid tax, TCAL Article 63 and Criminal Law Article 201 may apply, with the full suite of criminal fines and imprisonment for illegal tax reduction or evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The WFOE directors who authorize cross-border remittances without withholding may incur personal joint and several liability for the unpaid withholding and penalties based on complicity and false filings. The legal representative and directors face court-ordered travel bans, exit restrictions through the tax blacklist mechanism, seizure or freezing of personal assets if the corporate veil is pierced under PRC Company Law Article 23, and criminal prosecution as the persons directly in charge where the non-withholding is found to be intentional tax evasion rather than an ordinary error.
